title: Observed route regression
description: Every route reached by navigation stays reachable and keeps its stable landmarks.
test_strategy: Navigate (with the authorized login prelude when the route was only seen in-session); assert status and stable headings.

title: State-transition testing from observed transitions
description: Replay each observed control→state transition from a reproducible source state.
test_strategy: Only transitions whose source state is reachable by navigation and whose control was observed there.

title: Equivalence partitioning and boundary-value analysis
description: Partition each field's input space by its known rule and test each boundary (N-1, N, N+1) plus one representative per invalid class.
test_strategy: Rules come only from HTML declarations, explicit requirements or observed validation messages; unknown rules are reported, not invented.
oracle_strategy: OR-BROWSER-VALIDITY for browser-enforced rules; OR-ATTRIBUTABLE-FEEDBACK for requirement rules exercised server-side.
false_positive_warnings: type=tel or a free-text field has no implied rule

title: Server-side enforcement of declared constraints
description: Distinguish browser-native blocking from application behaviour: disable client validation and submit one value violating each declared constraint.
preconditions: Form submission is authorized on the target (GET forms are read-only and preferred)
test_strategy: One probe per field and rule kind, skipped when an explicit requirement already exercises the same field server-side.
oracle_strategy: OR-ATTRIBUTABLE-FEEDBACK; failures are likely defects because the HTML declaration is the only rule source.
safety: Submits data; local/authorized hosts only; counts against the mutation budget

title: Cross-field consistency (confirmation pairs)
description: When field semantics mark one field as the confirmation of another, test the 'values differ' row of the decision table.
test_strategy: All fields valid; confirmation = source + suffix; submit.
oracle_strategy: OR-ATTRIBUTABLE-FEEDBACK; semantic inference → likely defect unless a requirement states equality.

title: Ordering invariant for sortable collections
description: Records shown after choosing a sort option are monotone in the key the option names.

title: Metamorphic filter consistency
description: Every record displayed under a filter value carries that value.

title: Rendering-anomaly invariant after interactions
description: No interaction should render NaN, undefined, [object Object] or raw exception text.

title: Workflow sequence testing
description: Replay a multi-step workflow; for create forms, check the created record is reflected.

title: Regression tests from confirmed investigation findings
description: Replay a confirmed lead's recorded steps on observed selectors and assert the violated expectation.

title: Observed validation-message regression
description: Empty submissions whose validation message was observed during investigation.

title: Accessible-name audit per route
description: Compute accessible names for interactive controls on observed routes.

title: Domain scenario templates grounded on observed controls
description: Reusable domain scenarios (login, cart, checkout, CRUD) applied only when every step resolves to an observed control.

title: Pairwise combination testing
description: Cover all value pairs of interacting parameters with a minimal set.
limitations: Not automated: requires known parameter interactions

title: Repeated-action and idempotency testing
description: Repeat a submission and compare effects.

title: Per-record command takes effect
description: A command issued on one record of a list (a POST whose target names that record, e.g. cancel, archive, complete, remove) must remove or change that record; a success message alone is not evidence.
test_strategy: Open the list, snapshot the record that contains the command control, activate it, and compare the record after the response.
oracle_strategy: OR-RECORD-CHANGED: the record is absent or its content differs; identical content after the command is a likely defect (convention), never confirmed without a requirement.
false_positive_warnings: Commands that are read-only by nature (view, download, export, print, copy, share) are excluded
A command may legitimately be a no-op (already cancelled); the record must have exposed the command
safety: Changes one record per execution; only issued where the safety governor allows mutations
